results.name: The rubric endpoint returns exactly the 12 already-approved categories
Every criterion carries a real rule version
Every criterion carries min/max/weight (never invented — weight 1, range 0-10, matching the pre-existing behavior)
A partial draft (not every category scored) saves successfully
Reloading the entry rehydrates the real saved draft score
A final submission missing required criteria is rejected (server decides completeness)
A complete, valid submission is accepted
The weighted total is genuinely server-computed (8/10 across 12 equal-weight criteria = 80.00), never the fabricated client value
The scorecard is stamped with the real rubric rule version
A draft-save attempt against an already-submitted scorecard is rejected
Resubmitting with different scores never changes the immutable, already-submitted result
A draft save carrying an outdated expectedVersion is rejected with a real 409 conflict
Both requests of a rapid double-click (same idempotency key) resolve to the SAME real scorecard row
Of two concurrent FIRST-EVER draft saves for the same entry+judge, exactly one wins (200) and one honestly loses (409) — never two silently-created scorecards
Exactly one real scorecard row exists in the database despite the race
A judge not assigned to this entry cannot save a scorecard for it
golden_box_scorecard_draft_saved, golden_box_scorecard_submitted, and golden_box_entry_scored were all emitted
The canonical golden_box_entry_scored event carries the real server-computed weighted total
